differences.title: 1. REQUEST PIPELINE
differences.leftDesc: Axum builds handlers atop the Tower ecosystem: requests flow through composable middleware (services) and extractors, with explicit types guiding routing, validation, and response conversion at compile time.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify uses a hook/tap architecture: plugins register lifecycle hooks (e.g., preHandler/onSend). It composes handlers dynamically and relies on a highly optimized routing layer plus serialization-aware hooks.

differences.title: 2. TYPE SAFETY
differences.leftDesc: Axum’s extractors (e.g., Json, Path, Query) encode payload shapes in Rust types. Many failures become compile-time errors or deterministic runtime rejections without ad-hoc casts or loosely typed middleware.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify emphasizes schema-driven runtime validation: request/response JSON schemas can be checked per route. Type safety in Node is mostly provided by TypeScript tooling rather than framework-enforced compile-time types.

differences.title: 3. PERFORMANCE MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Axum runs on Rust with low overhead futures under Tokio. Handler execution avoids GC pauses, and data movement is controlled via ownership/borrowing, reducing allocations along the hot path.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify runs on Node’s single-threaded event loop with highly optimized HTTP parsing and response handling. Performance tuning focuses on minimizing allocations, using the fastest serializers, and controlling backpressure.

differences.title: 4. MIDDLEWARE COMPOSITION
differences.leftDesc: Tower layers let Axum stack cross-cutting concerns (auth, rate limiting, tracing) as strongly typed services. Middleware ordering and capabilities are expressed in trait bounds, not implicit runtime behavior.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify promotes composition through plugins and decorators. Plugins can add shared functionality (decorators) and register scoped hooks, enabling feature modularity while preserving encapsulation per server instance.

differences.title: 5. ERROR HANDLING
differences.leftDesc: Axum encourages returning Result types where error variants implement IntoResponse. This yields explicit mapping from errors to HTTP responses, and errors can carry structured data without throwing exceptions.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify uses explicit reply lifecycle control and error handlers: thrown errors are caught by the framework and routed to registered error handlers. It supports centralized formatting and per-route overrides with hooks.

differences.title: 6. ROUTING & EXTRACTORS
differences.leftDesc: Axum route handlers are composed of extractors that parse path/query/headers/body into typed values. This tight coupling reduces manual parsing and ensures consistent rejection behavior across endpoints.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify route definitions can pair handlers with JSON schema for input/output. Validation happens in the request lifecycle before handler execution, with Ajv-backed compilation for fast repeated checks.

differences.title: 7. ECOSYSTEM & OPERABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Axum integrates cleanly with Rust observability tools (e.g., tracing via tower-http). Middleware can emit spans/metrics with minimal overhead, and structured logs follow Rust’s type-safe formatting.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify integrates with Node observability via common middleware and ecosystem tooling (e.g., OpenTelemetry JS). Plugin scoping helps keep trace context consistent, while tooling around Node remains broadly standardized.
